title: Questions that must be answered before a decision — what we have, what we do not have, and how to find it
how_to_read: 'have' is evidence that exists in this repository or was read officially in this session, with a link.
'missing' is the information that does not exist. It is stated as missing, never filled with an estimate.
'how_to_discover' is the concrete route to obtain the missing information, and who can obtain it.
'clears_when' is the number that ends the debate. Where no number can be computed yet, it is blank.

status_values.answerable-now: the evidence in this repo plus an official read settles it
status_values.blocked-on-missing: cannot be answered until the named information exists
status_values.owner-decision: the facts are available; the choice is the owner's and has not been made

rows.question: How many 2026 NFL games are actually settled, and therefore how big is the backtest corpus?
rows.why_it_blocks: Every sample-size gate, every p-value and every '136-game log' reference depends on this one number.
rows.have: Two feeds say 137 finals (nfl-core results_feed_2026.csv FINAL rows; nfl-markets results_feed.csv 2026 rows). A transcription says 150 (nfl-marketboard results_2026_official.csv). The official standings read on 2026-11-19 gives 32 clubs, 300 team-games played, i.e. at most 150 completed games.
rows.missing: Which of the three feeds is reconciled line-by-line to the official game pages. nfl-core carries 137 finals and 272 total rows; the brief's '136' matches neither.
rows.how_to_discover: Reconcile nfl-core's 272 rows against the official week pages week by week (13 of 18 weeks have 14-16 scheduled games), and publish the count with the reconciled game list. The 150-row transcription should be compared against the same list.
rows.clears_when: One count, one file, every row linked to https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-N.

rows.question: Which of the three requirement registers is authoritative when they disagree on 62 statuses?
rows.why_it_blocks: If 'implemented' in one file and 'partial' in another both count, no readiness claim means anything.
rows.have: All three files exist and are counted: nfl-readiness-register (73 rows), nfl-req-review round 2 (73 rows), nfl-consolidated (73 rows). 21 rows agree, 29 disagree, 23 could not be matched by exact wording.
rows.missing: A rule that says which file wins, or a single file that all three defer to.
rows.how_to_discover: Adopt the round-2 rule already written in nfl-req-review ('met requires an existing artifact path and an official source'), because it is the only one of the three that states a testable condition, and retire the other two status columns to history.
rows.clears_when: One status column, one rule, and a verifier that fails when an 'implemented' row's evidence path does not resolve.

rows.question: Can a market line be published at all, or must every price stay blank?
rows.why_it_blocks: Without a market line there is no closing line value, no residual, no ROI — only a model talking to itself.
rows.have: No official NFL source publishes odds. The repository's own registers record this (FB-01 / DR-G1) and every price field in nfl-book is null by policy.
rows.missing: A licensed, timestamped pre-kickoff price series with terms that permit storage and publication of derived values.
rows.how_to_discover: Two routes, in order: (a) an operator or exchange API whose terms permit archival use; (b) a licensed historical odds vendor. Until one is signed, publish only model fair lines and label every market column THIRD-PARTY or blank.
rows.clears_when: One signed source, with its terms quoted in the repo, and open+close captured for every originated market.

rows.question: How often is the official injury report actually captured, and is that often enough to replay a week?
rows.why_it_blocks: A designation that is only captured once cannot show a Questionable→Out change, so no injury feature can be backtested without lookahead.
rows.have: Two captures in the repository: a rendered summary for Week 10 (2026-11-15T23:35Z) and a raw HTML capture for Week 11 (2026-11-18T23:49:17Z), both hashed in the readiness-register manifest. The brief asks for daily Wednesday-to-kickoff; the gap is visible.
rows.missing: Captures for 2026-11-19 through kickoff, and any capture at all for earlier weeks or seasons.
rows.how_to_discover: The scheduled capture workflow exists (nfl-readiness-register/capture/snapshot_official_pages.py). Run it on the Wed/Thu/Fri/satellite cadence and keep every file plus its hash; the manifest is already append-only.
rows.clears_when: At least three hashed captures per week for every week in the evaluation window, with zero unresolved schema drift.

rows.question: What share of injury-report rows carry a game-status designation, and does the brief's '6 of 254' hold?
rows.why_it_blocks: If almost no row carries a designation, then designation-based features are being trained on a handful of rows.
rows.have: Measured from the stored, hash-verified 2026-11-18 capture: 23 club tables, 242 player rows, 16 with a Game Status (9 Out, 7 Questionable), 226 blank. That is 6.6% designated — the same order as the brief's claim, but on a different copy.
rows.missing: A recount of the copy the brief used (254 rows, 6 designations) and a series across weeks so the share is not one snapshot.
rows.how_to_discover: Re-run nfl-desk/engine/parse_injuries.py over every stored capture, and start capturing earlier weeks. The brief's figure can then be reconciled against a dated file instead of a memory.
rows.clears_when: A per-week table of rows/designated/blank with the capture hash beside each count.

rows.question: Does 'Questionable' mean anything measurable?
rows.why_it_blocks: Every injury adjustment in a model rests on what the designation predicts. If it predicts nothing, the feature is noise.
rows.have: No. There is no inactive-list artifact anywhere in the repository, and no join from designation to whether the player played.
rows.missing: Official inactive lists (published about 90 minutes before kickoff) joined to designations, for several seasons.
rows.how_to_discover: Capture the official inactive list for every game from the game centre page, then join on player. The join is the whole feature; without it the label cannot be used.
rows.clears_when: At least 1,000 designation→inactive observations over three or more seasons, with a play-rate confidence interval per designation.

rows.question: Is depth order verified for all 32 clubs?
rows.why_it_blocks: The backup-deficiency feature, the matchup matrix and every depth-based strategy depend on knowing who is second and third string.
rows.have: A 32-club sweep exists: 31 clubs parsed from club pages, Houston published as an image and left blank rather than transcribed. One route (league depth paths) is closed.
rows.missing: A structured, dated source for Houston, and an as-of date for the 27 club pages that do not print one.
rows.how_to_discover: (a) ask the club for a text version, or (b) derive order from official snap counts if a source exists, or (c) use Game Books for actual starters. Do not build the feature until one route covers all 32.
rows.clears_when: 32/32 clubs with a dated, text-extractable depth chart, or an official snap-count source that covers the same ground.

rows.question: When a starter is out, did the backup actually replace him on the field?
rows.why_it_blocks: This is the difference between 'a replacement happened' and 'the replacement is a liability'. Only the second is a signal.
rows.have: Nothing official. No snap counts, no Game Book transcription, no confirmed starter list for any game.
rows.missing: Official snap counts or Game Book participation for the games in question.
rows.how_to_discover: NFL Game Books (official PDFs) print starters and participation. Capture them per game, then measure the replacement's share of snaps against the starter's season baseline.
rows.clears_when: Snap share for the replacement in every game where a starter was inactive, for a full season.

rows.question: Are the club depth charts stale against the official transactions log?
rows.why_it_blocks: A depth chart that still lists a player who is on injured reserve will name the wrong backup.
rows.have: The brief reports Baltimore still publishing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at QB after both went on IR and a replacement was traded in. A transactions artifact exists (nfl-readiness-register/data/transactions_nov2026.json).
rows.missing: A per-row 'last verified against transactions on <date>' column on the depth register, and a re-read of the club pages this session (none was performed).
rows.how_to_discover: Join every depth row to the reserve list and the transactions page; flag any row whose player appears on either after the row's as-of date.
rows.clears_when: Zero depth rows naming a player who is on reserve/injured reserve as of the row's own date.

rows.question: Is any strategy currently eligible for reward, and what would make one eligible?
rows.why_it_blocks: The whole point of the leaderboard is to pay skill, not luck. If nothing is eligible, that must be visible, not hidden.
rows.have: No. 15 strategy rows exist in nfl-lines/data/derived/leaderboard.json (copied with an added Wilson interval into nfl-arena/data/leaderboard_metrics.json); every one has eligible_for_reward false, and each carries its own luck verdict. The best sample is 303 bets with a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p of 0.44; the largest gate score is 5 of 8. The gates require a sample floor (n>=300 for a skill claim) and a multiplicity adjustment.
rows.missing: A prospective, pre-registered sample that survives the multiplicity gate.
rows.how_to_discover: Keep strategies in shadow, record every forecast before kickoff with its inputs, and let the sample accumulate. Do not re-tune a strategy mid-sample.
rows.clears_when: A pre-registered strategy reaching its own required n (1148–1290 bets at 80% power for the current effects) with a BH-adjusted p below the pre-set threshold and positive CLV.

rows.question: Does the model beat a naive baseline?
rows.why_it_blocks: If it does not, no amount of strategy work rescues it and the honest move is to publish that.
rows.have: A published walk-forward result: winner accuracy 0.5714 on 35 graded games against a 0.60 home-team baseline (one-sided p 0.70); totals MAE 15.12 vs 15.86 (permutation p 0.026) but failing the 300-game floor and the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.
rows.missing: A sample large enough to distinguish a small edge from noise, and an opponent-aware rating (the brief's own requirement).
rows.how_to_discover: Ingest the settled-game corpus with opponent adjustment, then re-run the same walk-forward with the same gates; the gates are already written and committed.
rows.clears_when: n≥300 graded games with a benchmark-relative proper score whose cluster bootstrap lower bound is above zero after multiplicity control.

rows.question: Are the published correlations officially sourced, and does each carry its n?
rows.why_it_blocks: A correlation from a third-party archive is not the same evidence as one from an official source, and a correlation without n cannot be weighted.
rows.have: nfl-markets publishes a third-party correlation group (covers/leg dependence) beside its official group; nfl-core has a correlations_n.csv; the NBA side reports n with every value. The brief asks for official sources only.
rows.missing: A rule that keeps third-party numbers off the same page as official ones, and n on every published value.
rows.how_to_discover: Split the page: official-source block and third-party block, each labelled, each with n and an interval. Compute from official results only where the official feed supports it.
rows.clears_when: Every published correlation row shows its n, its source type and its interval, and no third-party value appears unlabelled.

rows.question: Do the price snapshots contain real market opens and closes?
rows.why_it_blocks: If every market value is null, the 'residual against the market' is a residual against a blank.
rows.have: nfl-book holds 39 open/close rows (13 Week-11 games × side/total/moneyline) with every market value null by policy; the close value that does exist is a model run, not a market close. nfl-markets holds 12,573 rows from a third-party archive.
rows.missing: An official or licensed market series. Nothing else closes this.
rows.how_to_discover: Same route as Q03. Until then the snapshot store demonstrates the schema, not the market.
rows.clears_when: Non-null market open and close for every originated market, with source and capture time per row.

rows.question: Is row-level NFL data published within the terms of use?
rows.why_it_blocks: Publishing row-level official data without checking terms is the one mistake that could take the site down.
rows.have: A public static site publishing derived tables, and a repo holding raw captures. The NFL terms page is linked from the root portal but was not read line-by-line in this session.
rows.missing: A read of https://www.nfl.com/terms against what the site actually publishes, and a decision on the public/private split the brief already asks for.
rows.how_to_discover: Read the terms; list every published field; classify each as fact-of-the-game, derived, or league-published text; hold raw row-level data private until the classification is signed off.
rows.clears_when: A signed data policy row per published field, and no raw capture served publicly before that.

rows.question: Is the 2026 schedule announcement published beside the live schedule, as the brief requires?
rows.why_it_blocks: Totals and win-probability models need to know whether a fixture can still move, and the league publishes that in its own words.
rows.have: The Week 11 schedule read on 2026-11-19 prints the league's flexible-scheduling note for Weeks 16-18, the '2026 TBD Games' block, and a link to the flexible-scheduling procedures.
rows.missing: A dated copy of that announcement stored beside the schedule page, and the same for the season announcement.
rows.how_to_discover: Capture https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-11 and https://www.nfl.com/legal/flexible-scheduling-procedures with timestamps, and diff them weekly.
rows.clears_when: A stored, dated announcement beside every schedule page, with a diff column.

rows.question: Where is the fixture venue recorded, and can roof/surface be published?
rows.why_it_blocks: Totals and passing props move with wind and roof; publishing a stadium guess is worse than publishing nothing.
rows.have: The game centre for Colts at Texans prints Location HOUSTON, TX and Stadium RELIANT STADIUM (read 2026-11-19). Roof, surface and weather appear only in a third-party archive.
rows.missing: An official roof/surface designation and an official forecast overlay.
rows.how_to_discover: Venue facts come from the game centre. Roof designations are a stadium property that the league publishes in its stadium guide; forecast comes from the National Weather Service API. Both need a capture script and a citation per row.
rows.clears_when: Venue, roof and surface for all 32 stadiums with an official link per row, and an hourly forecast for each outdoor fixture.

rows.question: How would we know the site had become wrong?
rows.why_it_blocks: Forty namespaces publish overlapping claims with no cross-check, so a single stale number can sit on the site indefinitely.
rows.have: Each namespace has its own verifier and several pass. There is no verifier that compares namespaces with each other; this session added that comparison (62 status disagreements, four corpus counts, 40 flagged pages).
rows.missing: A single gate that fails when two published files disagree on the same fact.
rows.how_to_discover: Promote nfl-desk/engine/verify.py (this workspace) to the repo-level gate and extend it with the census comparisons; a disagreement becomes a build failure, not a paragraph.
rows.clears_when: One repo-level verifier that fails on cross-namespace disagreement, run on every push.

rows.question: What is the smallest change that makes this site usable for decisions?
rows.why_it_blocks: 40 landing pages and 40 flagged pages is not a decision surface; the owner cannot tell which page is current.
rows.have: A census of all 40 namespaces, their verifiers and their duplication. One entry point now exists (this workspace) and is linked from the root dashboard and the NFL portal.
rows.missing: A retirement decision: which namespaces are history and which are live.
rows.how_to_discover: Use the census table: keep the namespaces whose verifier passes and whose data a live page reads; mark the rest 'history' in a single column and stop linking them from the front door.
rows.clears_when: One front door, at most one live namespace per function, and every other namespace labelled history.
